When the company has a strong cost advantage over competitors
When raw material prices are falling

questionText: A supply chain manager notices that technology adoption by supply chain partners is inconsistent, creating data gaps. Which intervention is MOST effective?
options: Forcing all partners to use identical technology systems
Establishing data exchange standards, offering technology adoption support, and creating incentives for partners to share data consistently
Eliminating data-sharing requirements from supplier contracts
Developing manual workarounds for partners who do not adopt technology

questionText: A company is evaluating whether to implement a fully automated distribution center. Which financial and operational analysis is MOST essential before making this decision?
options: Comparing the design aesthetics of automated vs. manual facilities
Analyzing the return on investment, payback period, labor savings, throughput improvements, and impact on order fulfillment accuracy and speed
Benchmarking the number of robots used by competitors
Assessing employee satisfaction with manual processes

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes a "responsive" supply chain strategy and when it should be used?
options: A low-cost, high-efficiency supply chain used for commodity products with stable demand
A flexible, fast-reacting supply chain designed for products with unpredictable demand, short life cycles, or high variety, where speed and adaptability are more valuable than cost optimization
A supply chain focused exclusively on eliminating all supplier relationships
A supply chain that responds to government regulations only

questionText: A company is creating a new supply chain performance measurement framework. Which balanced set of metrics BEST captures overall supply chain health?
options: Only financial metrics such as cost and profit margin
A balanced scorecard including cost efficiency, delivery reliability, inventory performance, flexibility, sustainability, and customer service metrics
Only customer satisfaction scores
Only transportation metrics such as on-time delivery rate

questionText: A supply chain manager must design a supply chain for a product that will be sold globally, involves multiple tiers of suppliers, and must meet stringent environmental regulations. Which design principle is MOST critical?
options: Minimizing the number of suppliers to simplify management
Building a transparent, compliant, and collaborative multi-tier supply chain with end-to-end visibility, robust supplier qualification processes, and integrated sustainability standards
Concentrating all manufacturing in the cheapest region regardless of regulatory requirements
Delaying compliance with environmental regulations until they become mandatory

questionText: The "SCOR model" (Supply Chain Operations Reference) is a framework used to:
options: Design marketing campaigns for supply chain companies
Describe, benchmark, and improve supply chain processes across plan, source, make, deliver, return, and enable activities
Regulate international trade between countries
Calculate the optimal reorder point for inventory

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "supply chain disruption"?
options: A company renegotiating a supplier contract for better pricing
A major earthquake damaging a key supplier's factory, halting production and causing significant delays
A supplier delivering goods one day earlier than scheduled
A logistics provider switching to a more fuel-efficient vehicle fleet

questionText: The concept of "supply chain resilience" refers to the ability of a supply chain to:
options: Operate at the lowest possible cost under normal conditions
Anticipate, adapt to, and recover rapidly from unexpected disruptions while maintaining continuous operations
Resist all forms of change or innovation
Operate without any reliance on technology

questionText: A supply chain manager is reviewing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Which KPI MOST directly measures supply chain customer service performance?
options: Total warehousing cost per unit
Order fill rate and perfect order percentage
Number of suppliers in the network
Total landed cost per shipment

questionText: "Supply chain collaboration" between a buyer and supplier is MOST effective when:
options: The buyer holds all the negotiating power and dictates terms to the supplier
Both parties share risks and rewards, exchange information openly, and align their objectives to create mutual value
The supplier manages all aspects of the buyer's inventory
The buyer and supplier operate completely independently with minimal communication

questionText: A company is experiencing high inventory levels despite having good demand forecasts. The MOST likely root cause is:
options: The company's warehouse is too large
Poor supply chain coordination, excessive safety stock policies, or infrequent ordering cycles that do not align with actual demand signals
The company's products are too popular
The demand forecast is too accurate

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a "supply chain audit"?
options: To calculate the annual bonuses of supply chain employees
To systematically evaluate supply chain processes, compliance, performance, and risks to identify improvement opportunities
To review the company's financial statements for tax purposes
To assess the company's marketing strategy

questionText: When designing a global supply chain, which factor is MOST likely to increase supply chain complexity?
options: Using a single transportation mode for all shipments
Operating across multiple countries with different regulations, cultures, currencies, and infrastructure quality levels
Selling a single standardized product globally
Using a single centralized distribution center

questionText: A company's supply chain strategy must be aligned with its overall business strategy. A company competing on product innovation and speed-to-market should design its supply chain to prioritize:
options: Maximum cost efficiency and minimum investment in new capabilities
Agility, flexibility, and rapid new product introduction capabilities that can quickly respond to changing market requirements
Long-term fixed supply contracts to lock in low prices
Centralized decision-making to control all supply chain costs

questionText: In a scenario where a company's supply chain faces increasing complexity due to expanding product lines and global operations, which organizational response is MOST appropriate?
options: Reducing product lines to simplify the supply chain
Investing in integrated supply chain management capabilities including advanced technology, skilled talent, and organizational structures that support cross-functional coordination
Outsourcing all supply chain activities to eliminate internal complexity
Restricting expansion to domestic markets only

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "strategic supply chain decision"?
options: Deciding the daily shift schedule for warehouse staff
Choosing whether to build a new distribution center, outsource logistics, or enter a long-term partnership with a 3PL provider
Selecting the font for supplier invoices
Determining the daily reorder quantity for a single product

questionText: Supply chain network design decisions typically involve trade-offs between:
options: Employee salaries and marketing budgets
Transportation costs, inventory holding costs, facility costs, and customer service levels
Product design complexity and packaging materials
Number of employees and office space requirements

questionText: Which of the following describes a "supply chain strategy" that prioritizes lean principles?
options: Investing in excess capacity and inventory to handle all possible demand scenarios
Systematically eliminating waste, reducing lead times, and optimizing flow to deliver maximum value to customers at minimum cost
Expanding the supplier base as widely as possible
Producing all products in-house regardless of cost

questionText: A company that has achieved excellent supply chain efficiency suddenly faces a competitor offering faster delivery and more product customization. To respond effectively, the company should:
options: Cut prices further to compete on cost
Reassess its supply chain strategy and invest in responsive capabilities such as flexible manufacturing, postponement, and faster replenishment
Reduce its product range to simplify operations
Exit markets where the competitor is present

questionText: The PRIMARY reason supply chains fail to achieve their performance objectives is often:
options: Too many suppliers in the network
Poor coordination, misaligned incentives, lack of information sharing, and organizational silos that prevent effective collaboration
Excessive investment in supply chain technology
Overly generous customer service commitments

questionText: A company is developing a supply chain risk management plan. Which step should come FIRST?
options: Purchasing supply chain insurance
Identifying and categorizing potential risks across the supply chain, including supply, operational, demand, and environmental risks
Implementing new technology to track shipments
Negotiating risk-sharing clauses in all supplier contracts

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between supply chain management and competitive advantage?
options: Supply chain management is purely an operational function with no strategic value

Effective supply chain management can create competitive advantage through superior cost efficiency, service quality, speed, flexibility, and sustainability that are difficult for competitors to replicate
Competitive advantage in supply chain management is achieved solely through having the lowest purchase prices
Supply chain management only affects operational efficiency, not market competitiveness

questionText: A supply chain coordinator is working to improve inter-organizational collaboration. Which action is MOST critical for success?
options: Issuing strict penalties to suppliers who fail to meet targets
Building trust through transparent communication, shared performance metrics, joint problem-solving, and equitable risk and reward sharing
Reducing the frequency of communication to avoid information overload
Limiting information sharing to protect competitive intelligence

questionText: Which of the following outcomes is MOST indicative of a well-integrated and high-performing supply chain?
options: Low supplier diversity and high concentration risk
High order fill rates, low total supply chain cost, short lead times, and strong supplier relationships that enable continuous improvement
Maximum inventory levels at all points in the supply chain
All supply chain decisions made exclusively by corporate headquarters

questionText: A new graduate joining a logistics and supply chain management team should first focus on understanding:
options: The company's advertising strategy
The end-to-end supply chain structure, key processes, performance metrics, and how their role contributes to overall supply chain objectives
The company's HR policies and salary structure
The design of the company's website

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST accurate description of the "supply chain lifecycle"?
options: The time it takes for a product to be manufactured
The full sequence of activities from raw material extraction through production, distribution, consumption, and end-of-life product management
The duration of a supplier contract
The product warranty period offered to customers

questionText: A supply chain manager is assessing two distribution strategies: direct-to-consumer (D2C) vs. through intermediaries. Which factor MOST favors a D2C strategy?
options: Low product value and wide geographic distribution
High-margin products, direct customer relationships, need for customization, and the ability to capture customer data for supply chain optimization
The presence of many established intermediaries in the market
High transportation costs for small parcel delivery

questionText: Which of the following supply chain activities falls under the "source" process in the SCOR model?
options: Manufacturing finished goods
Procuring materials and components from suppliers, including supplier selection, ordering, and supplier relationship management
Delivering goods to end customers
Managing returns from customers

questionText: In supply chain management, "service level" refers to:
options: The quality of food served in the company cafeteria
The probability of meeting customer demand from available inventory, or the percentage of orders fulfilled completely and on time
The grade of transportation service selected for shipments
The level of customer service training provided to warehouse staff

questionText: A company is expanding into a new international market and must extend its supply chain. Which factor represents the GREATEST risk to be managed?
options: The new market's local cuisine preferences
Unfamiliar regulatory requirements, customs procedures, currency risks, political instability, and the challenge of finding reliable local logistics partners
The local market's preference for a different product color
The availability of office space for the company's local team

questionText: Supply chain "agility" and supply chain "efficiency" are BEST described as:
options: Synonymous terms that describe the same supply chain characteristic
Complementary but often conflicting objectives — efficiency focuses on cost minimization through standardization and scale, while agility focuses on speed and flexibility to respond to change
Both measures of transportation speed in the supply chain
Both measures of inventory accuracy in the supply chain

questionText: A supply chain analyst discovers that inventory turnover is declining while demand is stable. Which supply chain issue does this MOST likely indicate?
options: The company is growing rapidly and adding new products
Excess inventory is accumulating, possibly due to poor demand forecasting, overly conservative safety stock policies, or supply chain coordination failures
The company's transportation network is becoming more efficient
Customer service levels are improving significantly

questionText: In supply chain design, "postponement" and "speculation" represent two opposing strategies. When is "speculation" (building to forecast) MOST appropriate?
options: When products are highly customized and demand is unpredictable
When demand is stable and predictable, economies of scale in production are significant, and lead times for customization are too long to satisfy customers
When product variety is extremely high and each customer requires a unique product
When all customers require immediate delivery of unique customized products

questionText: A supply chain manager has been asked to assess the environmental impact of the company's logistics operations. Which metric is MOST relevant to this assessment?
options: Total number of delivery trucks in the fleet
Carbon emissions per unit delivered, fuel consumption efficiency, and percentage of shipments using low-emission transportation modes
Total number of deliveries completed per day
Number of logistics staff employed

questionText: When implementing supply chain improvements, which change management principle is MOST critical for ensuring that improvements are sustained?
options: Making all changes as quickly as possible without involving staff
Engaging supply chain employees and partners in the change process, providing training, setting clear performance expectations, and monitoring progress consistently
Implementing all technology changes simultaneously to minimize disruption
Delegating all change management responsibilities to external consultants

questionText: A company's supply chain is described as "fragile." This MOST likely means:
options: The supply chain uses delicate packaging materials
The supply chain lacks redundancy, flexibility, and risk mitigation measures, making it highly vulnerable to disruptions that can cascade into major performance failures
The supply chain operates exclusively with small and medium suppliers
The supply chain has too many distribution tiers

questionText: In supply chain management, "demand shaping" refers to:
options: Changing the physical shape of products to reduce shipping costs
Using pricing, promotions, and other incentives to influence customer demand to better align with supply capabilities
Reshaping the demand forecast after actual demand is known
Training customers to place orders in a specific format

questionText: A supply chain manager must present a business case for a new supply chain initiative to senior management. Which element is MOST essential for a compelling business case?
options: A detailed technical description of the technology to be implemented
A clear articulation of the problem being solved, quantified benefits, costs, implementation risks, and return on investment
A list of all supply chain textbooks that support the initiative
A comparison of the company's supply chain with its best-performing supplier

questionText: Which of the following supply chain practices BEST illustrates the concept of "co-creation" between a buyer and supplier?
options: The buyer imposing cost reduction targets on the supplier without collaboration
The buyer and supplier jointly designing products, processes, or systems to create mutual value, share knowledge, and improve overall supply chain performance
The buyer allowing the supplier to set all contract terms
The supplier producing all products without any input from the buyer

questionText: A supply chain manager is evaluating whether to implement vendor-managed inventory (VMI). Which condition MOST supports adopting VMI?
options: The buyer and supplier have a poor relationship with limited trust
The supplier has better visibility into the buyer's demand patterns, and a collaborative relationship exists where the supplier can manage replenishment more efficiently than the buyer
The buyer's demand is highly unpredictable and there is no historical sales data
The product is a high-value, low-volume item with long lead times

questionText: In supply chain operations, the "make-or-buy" decision should be guided PRIMARILY by:
options: The preference of the CEO for insourcing
Analysis of core competencies, total cost comparison, strategic risk, quality requirements, and capacity considerations
Which option requires fewer employees
Which option was used by the company in the previous year

questionText: A company wants to reduce the total cost of its supply chain without compromising customer service. Which lever MOST comprehensively addresses this goal?
options: Reducing customer service commitments to cut delivery costs
Implementing end-to-end supply chain optimization that simultaneously addresses demand forecasting accuracy, inventory positioning, transportation efficiency, and supplier performance
Switching to cheaper suppliers regardless of quality
Eliminating all safety stock to reduce holding costs

questionText: In the context of supply chain management, "total delivered cost" includes:
options: Only the purchase price of goods from suppliers
All costs associated with acquiring and delivering goods to the customer, including purchase price, transportation, customs duties, warehousing, handling, and quality-related costs
Only transportation and warehousing costs
Only the cost of the product at the point of manufacture

questionText: A supply chain is described as "integrated." This MOST accurately means:
options: The supply chain uses a single technology platform for all operations
Supply chain partners share information, coordinate activities, and align their objectives to function as a unified system, minimizing inefficiencies across organizational boundaries
All supply chain activities are performed by a single company
The supply chain operates exclusively within one country

questionText: A supply chain manager in Ethiopia is designing a supply chain for industrial goods that must be imported. Which supply chain challenge is MOST specific to the Ethiopian context?
options: High customer demand for product customization
Infrastructure constraints, customs clearance procedures, foreign exchange availability, and limited logistics service provider capacity that may increase lead times and total landed costs
Oversupply of skilled logistics professionals in the local market
Excessive competition among domestic logistics providers
